claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 has a metastable high-temperature BCC state.
Rapid quenching from above 1200°C produces a single-phase BCC structure in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Rapid quenching preserves the metastable high-temperature BCC state.
A composition-dependent free-energy driving force promotes local elemental partitioning in the alloy.
The free-energy driving force promotes short-range chemical ordering involving Al and Cr.
Sluggish diffusion of Al and Cr kinetically limits the development of short-range order.
Short-range-order clusters form only after a critical time-temperature threshold is reached.
Al–Cr short-range-order clusters act as precursors to nucleation of an ordered secondary phase.
Short-range-order clusters reduce the nucleation barrier for the ordered secondary phase.
Annealing can transform the metastable BCC state into a dual-phase microstructure containing residual BCC and an ordered B2 or L12 phase.
The transformation rate and extent are determined by the balance between the thermodynamic driving force for ordering and atomic-diffusion kinetics.
Annealing between 650°C and 750°C provides activated diffusion while retaining kinetic control over elemental rearrangement.
Changing the Al concentration by 1–2 at.% will modulate the thermodynamic driving force.
During annealing, detectable short-range order will appear before nucleation of the ordered secondary phase.
Increasing annealing time or temperature within the specified window will promote nucleation of B2 or L12 alongside the residual BCC matrix.
Rapidly quenched baseline samples will remain single-phase BCC in the absence of subsequent thermal activation.
Transformation under annealing but not in the quenched baseline would show that thermal treatment kinetically activates the transformation.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply only for annealing at 650–750°C for 1–100 hours.
Secondary-phase nucleation under conditions too diffusion-limited to support short-range order would falsify the mechanism.
A phase transformation occurring without detectable short-range-order clusters would falsify the mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary field says transformations below 650°C are outside the hypothesis's defined domain, while the falsification experiment uses such below-boundary transformations as evidence that would falsify the hypothesis.
The boundary field treats transformation in the complete absence of SRO as outside the defined boundary, whereas the falsification rule treats transformation without SRO as a decisive falsifier.
